Hi Sandeep — thanks for the clear list. I attached a current subprocessor roster and a high-level telemetry dataflow diagram to this reply. Quick answers up front:  

- Roster: included (redwood_subprocessors_20250409.csv). It includes role, region, SOC2 status, and data access scope.
- Telemetry: we collect service-level metrics and tracing for the serving runtime; request-level metadata (request id, model id, latency, error codes) are retained for 90 days. We do not persist raw prompt/response text at token level for customer requests by default — only anonymized usage buckets unless the customer opts into log retention for troubleshooting.
- Caching: ephemeral KV cache lives on node memory; no persistent storage of cached content beyond service restart.
- KMS / keys: production customer keys are managed via customer KMS integrations (BYOK or Redwood-managed keys). For Redwood-managed keys, keys are stored in AWS KMS with regional residency options; cross-region replication is not enabled by default.
- Onboarding controls: subprocessors must complete our security onboarding checklist, provide SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, and submit a data processing attestation. We maintain vendor evidence in a restricted drive and CMDB (tracker attached).

I'll flag the items that typically require follow-up: token-level logs (we'll need a signed DPA amendment if a customer requests full-text retention), and any KMS key escrow / split access requests (ops + security review).

If you're available Thu 9:30am PT I can walk through the attachments — otherwise I can extract the specific columns you want and send a redline-friendly package.

Regards,

Sandeep — answers inline below, and a couple of action items for evidence handoff.

1) Derived identifiers: we do not persist hashed prompt tokens or partial transcripts in normal operation. We generate request hashes (non-reversible identifiers) for dedup/analytics; those hashes cannot be used to reconstruct prompt text. If a customer requests hashed prompt retention for troubleshooting, we require a specific justification and DPA amendment.

2) Third-party libraries: our runtime uses open-source telemetry libraries (OpenTelemetry) and an internally managed ingestion pipeline. We do not ship crash dumps or prompt text to third-party SaaS vendors. Hosted monitoring vendors receive aggregated service metrics only (no request text). Details are in the telemetry diagram attachment.

3) EU platform infra providers: these vendors operate orchestration and node provisioning in EU regions. They do not have access to customer KMS keys or plaintext telemetry; access is limited to anonymized service metrics and node-level health metrics. We enforce role-based access control and ephemeral SSH sessions logged to our audit service (see JIRA SEC-4823 for audit trails).

Action items / evidence we can share now:  
- The attached CSV (same as before) with an additional column for "evidence_location" pointing to Drive links and the CMDB folder.
- Telemetry diagram (attached) showing where PII/Text is redacted or not persisted.
- We can produce a filtered log sample (redacted) under NDA for tooling verification — will need an evidence request form signed.

Next steps: I created a short ticket (JIRA:SEC-4823) and uploaded the evidentiary PDFs to the Driver folder. If Bridgewell can sign the evidence-request form we will push a redacted log sample and the vendor SOC 2 certs.
